title: अग्नि महाकाव्यमा दलित उत्पीडन र प्रतिरोधको विमर्श [Dalit Subjugation and Resistance in the Epic Agni]
nepali: नवराज लम्सालको अग्नि (२०७८) महाकाव्य दलित समस्याको केन्द्रीयतामा रचिएको हुँदा यहाँ सोही कोणबाट विमर्श गरिएको छ । दलित साहित्य सिद्धान्तका आधारमा विमर्श गरिएको हुँदा यसको विमर्श पद्धति मूलतः निगमनात्मक विधिमा आधारित छ । यसको विषय विश्लेषण गुणात्मक शोधको ढाँचामा छ । यसका आधार र सैद्धान्तिक सामग्री पुस्तकालयबाट लिइएका हुँदा सामग्रीको स्रोत भने पुस्तकालय हो । गैरदलितले दलित समस्याकेन्द्री रचना लेख्नु आफैमा निकै चुनौतीपूर्ण विषय भए पनि नेपाली महाकाव्य परम्परामा यस महाकाव्यको रचना निकै सार्थक बनेको छ किनभने यसमा दलितको लुप्तप्रायः इतिहासलाई नवइतिहासवादी कोणबाट उत्खनन गरी बुनिएको छ । जातीय विभेदमा आधारित उत्पीडनका कारण दलित साहित्यमा धेरैजसो देखिने दलितका आवेग, आक्रोश र विद्रोहका चर्का रूप यसमा नदेखिए पनि गैरदलित महाकाव्यकारको सुधारवादी दृष्टिकोणकै परिधिमै यसमा संयमित आवेग, आक्रोश र प्रतिरोध चेतना आएका छन् । तिनको अभिव्यक्ति ठुले कामी, छेलाङी विश्वकर्मा र जुनीमायामार्फत गरिएको छ । ऐतिहासिक पात्र ठुले कामीमा प्रतिरोध चेतना रहे पनि उनले उत्पीडक सामु व्यक्त गर्न सकेका छैनन् तर मर्ने बोलामा छोरा सामु तीप्रतिको घृणा भाव व्यक्त गर्दै सन्तानलाई सचेत त बनाएका छन् । वर्तमान समयका छेलाङी र जुनीमायाले भने तार्किक ढङ्गमै प्रतिरोध गरेका छन् । छेलाङीको प्रतिरोधमा बौद्धिकता र तार्किकता बढी पाइन्छ भने जुनीमायाको प्रतिरोधमा व्यावहारिकता बढी देखिएको छ । आप्mनो उत्पीडनप्रति गरिएको दलितको यही संयमित प्रतिरोध चेतनाले महाकाव्य सामयिक र आकर्षक बनेको छ । [Naba Raj Lamsal’s epic Agni (2078 BS) has been interpreted from the Dalit perpective. The study adopts the deductive research method to discuss the epic, which is based on the theories of Dalit literature, using the qualitative research design. The study depends on the secondary sources retrieved from the library, using both print and e-resources. Although there are challenges to study on the Dalit issues as the theme of the epic which is created by an author who belongs to a caste other than the Dalit, the epic has reclaimed the subjugated history of Dalits that is portrayed from the neo-historist point of view. The epic has brought out the suppression of minority people like the Dalits, dealing with inner awareness such as emotions, resentments and protests. Such awareness of resistance is expressed through the characters like Thule Kami, Chhelangi Bishwokarma, and Junimaya. Despite the fact that the characters have the awareness of resistance, but in the case of Thule Kami who is a subaltern character cannot express his suppression though he tells his son to be aware of casteism at his death bed. However, Chhelangi and Junimaya have resisted the urge to alter the casteism related discriminations. Whereas Chhelangi’s resistance is driven by intellect and logic, Junimaya’s resistance is driven by practicality. Thus, the balanced portrayal of characters has popularized the epic and has become a historical document for the Dalit writing in Nepal.]
american_english: Naba Raj Lamsal's epic Agni (2078 BS) is composed with the centrality of Dalit problems, so here it has been discussed from that same angle. Since the discussion is based on Dalit literature theory, its method of discussion is mainly based on the deductive method. Its subject analysis is in the framework of qualitative research. Since its bases and theoretical materials are taken from the library, the source of material is the library. Although a non-Dalit writing a Dalit-centered work is itself a highly challenging subject, in the Nepali epic tradition the composition of this epic has become highly meaningful because in it the nearly lost history of Dalits has been excavated and woven from a neo-historicist angle. Although the sharp forms of Dalit emotion, anger and rebellion mostly seen in Dalit literature because of oppression based on caste discrimination are not seen here, within the very perimeter of the reformist perspective of the non-Dalit epic poet, restrained emotion, anger and resistance consciousness have come into this. Their expression has been made through Thule Kami, Chhelangi Vishwakarma and Junimaya. Although the historical character Thule Kami has resistance consciousness, he has not been able to express it before the oppressor, but on his deathbed before his son he has expressed hatred towards it and at least made his offspring aware. The present-day Chhelangi and Junimaya, however, have resisted in a logical manner. In Chhelangi's resistance more intellect and logic are found, whereas in Junimaya's resistance more practicality is seen. This very restrained resistance consciousness of Dalits towards their own oppression has made the epic timely and attractive.

informal_english: Navraj Lamsal's epic Agni (2078 BS) is built around Dalit problems, so here we've discussed it from that same angle. The discussion is based on Dalit literature theory, so the method is mainly deductive. The subject analysis is in qualitative research framework. The bases and theoretical material come from the library, so the source of material is the library. It's a hectic challenge for a non-Dalit to write a Dalit-centred work, but in the Nepali epic tradition this epic has turned out really meaningful, because it digs up and weaves the nearly lost history of Dalits from a neo-historicist angle. The sharp forms of Dalit emotion, anger and rebellion you mostly see in Dalit literature because of caste-based oppression aren't really here, but within the reformist perspective of the non-Dalit epic poet, restrained emotion, anger and resistance consciousness have come through. They're expressed through Thule Kami, Chhelangi Vishwakarma and Junimaya. Thule Kami, the historical character, has resistance consciousness but couldn't express it before the oppressor; on his deathbed before his son he expressed hatred towards it and at least made his kids aware. The present-day Chhelangi and Junimaya, though, resisted in a logical way. Chhelangi's resistance has more intellect and logic, while Junimaya's has more practicality. This restrained resistance consciousness of Dalits towards their own oppression is what's made the epic timely and attractive.
